name: kernel_start
why: Version 1 (protocol.json, addenda) showed by stall sampling that on H100 a uniform-path constant load (ULDC) whose line is not resident holds its warp at the load itself, one load after the other, while the engine lets the load issue and makes only its readers wait; a register-indexed LDC behaves as the engine models it. Version 1 could not install anything: its clock criterion was unusable (filler noise, MEMBAR in the probe), and installing the hold with today's latency (406.5 per line) would overshoot hardware (about 150 per bank-0 line at 8 warps per CTA). Version 2 measures the hold per line with the instrument that worked (per-pc stall sampling), for a cold and a resident line, per bank and per number of warps of the CTA, and installs rule and values together. B300 is not in version 2: it has no stall-sampling path for probe kernels yet.
data_seen_before_freezing: Everything listed in protocol.json and its addenda, in particular: u.b0.n4.f0 at g132.w8 holds 152 / 135 / 103 / 145 cycles per warp on four ULDCs of four different bank-0 lines (the pointer-parameter ULDC before them 152), readers 0-15; u.b3.n4.f0 holds 631-750 per line; clocks M for four uniform bank-0 lines 325 (g1.w1), 384 (g132.w1), 741 (g132.w8), 736 (g528.w8), the eight warps of a CTA within 668-836; uniform bank 3 3400-4400.
No measurement of a resident uniform line exists in this protocol's data. constant_launch v3 reports a uniform second traversal of 68.0 cycles per load (dependent chain, clock after every load).

probe.kernel: Every thread of every warp runs the same straight-line code, no thread-id dependent branch before the last clock, no MEMBAR, no filler. t0 = clock; group 1: 16 uniform loads x_k = T[s + 64 k], k = 0..15 (16 different 64 B lines of the 4096 B table, s a warp-uniform non-constant offset below 16); group 2: 16 uniform loads z_k = T[x_k]; group 3: 16 uniform loads w_k = T[z_k]; y = sum of w_k; t1 = clock; lane 0 of every warp stores t0, t1, y. The table holds T[i] = i, so groups 2 and 3 read the lines group 1 read (resident by then) through an index that is not a compile-time constant.
probe.banks: 0: by-value kernel parameter struct of 4096 B; 3: 4096 B __constant__ array written once before the first launch.
probe.shapes: W = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 warps per CTA, with the grid chosen so that every row has at least 1056 warps and every CTA is in the first wave (the sample count of a row follows its warp count; version 1: 2759 samples for 1056 warps over 1484 cycles): W = 1 grid 1056, W = 2 grid 528, W = 4 grid 264, W = 8 grid 132, W = 16 grid 132. This rests on version 1's observation that the CTAs per SM do not change the hold (four uniform bank-0 lines: 741 at g132.w8, 736 at g528.w8); control rows W = 8 grid 528 repeat that check on this probe (when they differ from W = 8 grid 132 by more than 10 % in H_cold, the W axis is not installed and the finding is reported). Clocks only: g1.w1.
probe.launches: 4 launches per process; launch 0 and launch 2 measured.
probe.sass_gate: between the two clock reads exactly 48 ULDC with a UR index on the cell's bank; the index register of every group-2 load is the destination of one group-1 load, of every group-3 load the destination of one group-2 load, each group-1 destination used exactly once; no MEMBAR, no other memory instruction between the clocks. A cell failing the gate is recorded and not measured; the probe may be rewritten to pass, every tried form recorded.

runner.stall_sampling: cyclescope reference --metrics --source-stalls, sampling interval 0, reference conditions (--cache-control all), launch pinned to the traced launch; rows in suites/hopper/microbench, set `kstart2`: 2 cells x 6 shapes (the five W and the control) x 2 launches = 24 rows, each measured twice (reference-a, reference-b) and replayed with --stall-ledger. Output $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/h100-v2.
runner.clocks: the same binary under ncu with the reference conditions, two runs, all 7 shapes: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/kernel_start/h100-v2/run-{a,b}, raw.tsv with one line per warp (t0, t1, y).

derivation.sampling: per row and pass, cycles per warp (all classes but selected) on each of the 48 ULDC pcs and on every other pc between the two clock reads. cold(k) = group-1 load k, resident(k) = the group-2 and group-3 loads of line k. H_cold = mean of cold(k) over k = 1..15 (load 0 is reported apart: it follows the kernel's own parameter loads); H_res = mean over the 32 group-2 / group-3 loads; other = the sum on the non-load pcs between the clocks; share = (sum on the 48 loads) / (that sum + other).
derivation.clocks: D = median over warps of t1 - t0; check: D against the row's sampled sum on the pcs between the clocks plus their issue cycles.
derivation.usable: a row with at least 2000 samples in both passes whose two passes agree within 10 % on H_cold (and within 10 % or 3 cycles on H_res); a shape whose launch-0 row is unusable has no value.

outcomes_before_data.rule: Per bank, on the usable launch-0 rows: when share >= 0.7 on every usable shape (at least three shapes usable, W = 8 among them), the engine rule is installed for that bank class: a uniform-path constant load whose line is not resident in the SM's constant cache when it issues holds its warp at issue for the cold hold, the line is resident from the end of the hold, and the load's result is ready at the end of the hold; ledger reason `constant_hold`. A uniform load of a resident line: when H_res < 3 cycles the load adds nothing (result ready at issue); else it holds at issue for H_res when the resident loads' own share is >= 0.7, and keeps today's result-latency treatment with H_res as its latency otherwise. Bank class: bank 0 from cell b0, every other bank from cell b3.
outcomes_before_data.values: memory.constant_cache, new fields (source kernel_start.h100.v2): uniform_bank0_cold_hold_cycles and uniform_cold_hold_cycles = H_cold as a function of the CTA's launch warps (axis launch_warps_per_cta, linear between the measured W; mean of the two passes), evidence `measured` when every installed W is usable, `experimental` and not installed otherwise; uniform_resident_cycles = H_res at W = 8 (one value for both banks when the two banks agree within 10 % or 3 cycles, else per bank class). The vector path and every existing field are untouched; uniform loads stop using miss / hit / same_line.
outcomes_before_data.reported_only: launch 2 against launch 0; load 0; the spread of t1 - t0 over the warps of a CTA; g1.w1 clocks; the replay's ledger on the same rows before the change.

install: One semantic commit: schema field(s), generated schema, h100 leaf values, engine rule, fixture test of the hold (ledger reason, serial holds, resident line). b300 keeps today's behaviour (fields absent -> rule off). Then the h100 full-GPU ledgers and the comparison are re-run; judged by the site table (constant-load pcs, code outside loops) and the imc_miss totals, with the cycle error reported next to it. If the site error of the code outside loops gets worse on H100, the change is reverted and reported.
not_allowed: No change to thresholds, shapes or derivation after data; no value from a full-GPU case; no rule for a bank class whose own cell does not meet the condition; nothing for b300.

addenda.when: after six probe builds, before any clock or sampling data
addenda.text: The gate as written cannot be met: the offset s must come from a load of the kernel's pointer parameter, and ptxas places that load (`ULDC UR, c[0x0][0x1210]`, absolute address, no register index) after the first clock read; every way tried of consuming s before the clock turns the whole chain into register-indexed LDC ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/kernel_start/h100-v2/build/gate_failures.md). The first build has the 48 loads with the declared dependence and nothing else but that one load. Gate amended: between the two clock reads exactly 48 ULDC with a UR index on the cell's bank as declared, plus exactly one ULDC of bank 0 with an absolute address (the pointer parameter), issued before the 48; nothing else changes (no MEMBAR, no other memory instruction). Derivation amended accordingly: that load is reported apart as `seed` and is in neither the 48-load sum nor `other`; H_cold, H_res, share and the outcomes are as declared.

addenda.when: h100 run (24 sampling rows twice, clocks twice; probe 5d9959db) — results and what is installed
addenda.text: Data: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/kernel_start/h100-v2 (reference-a / -b, sim), $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/kernel_start/h100-v2/raw.tsv. 23 of 24 rows usable (b3 g528.w8 launch 0: the passes give 437 / 503); every row has 3700-8400 samples. Share of the wait on the 48 loads: 0.89-0.98 (b0), 0.95-0.99 (b3), class imc_miss throughout -> the rule condition is met for both bank classes. H_cold per line, launch 0, W = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16: bank 0 116.6 / 119.9 / 119.3 / 120.2 / 120.2; bank 3 443.1 / 478.3 / 473.7 / 465.3 / 456.7 (first bank-3 load of the kernel 710-1100). Control (W = 8, grid 528 against grid 132): bank 0 115.0 against 120.2; bank 3 has no usable launch-0 control (launch 2: 441.4 against 459.3). H_res (second and third read of the same 16 addresses, 4 KiB apart in total): bank 0 124-131, bank 3 194-216; these loads hold too (their own share above 0.9). Launch 2 equals launch 0 within 5 %. Clocks: t1 - t0 for the 49 loads 6430-7170 (bank 0) and 13800-16200 (bank 3) on every multi-CTA shape, consistent with the sampled sums; at g1.w1 2755-3143 and 11300-15100. Reading: on bank 0 a first touch costs what a later touch costs (about 120, the size of the installed hit latency 107): the parameter bank is not cold at launch, and what the samples call imc_miss is the latency of a uniform read outside a small recently-used set, charged at the load. Bank 3 has a real first-touch cost (about 465, installed miss 406.5) and about 200 afterwards. Two limits found in the data: (1) the shapes kept at least 8 warps per SM in every row, so the W axis as run shows no dependence, while one warp on one SM is about half as slow per load (g1.w1 clocks 57 per load; version 1 at one warp per SM 77 per line): the values hold for 8 or more warps per SM, which is what full-GPU launches have. (2) The probe's `resident` loads are all outside the 2 KiB range in which the crossings protocol measured 37 cycles; hardware-only over the full-GPU reference, bank-0 ULDCs executed repeatedly per warp carry 7.5 cycles of imc_miss per execution (those executed once: 51). Applying H_res to every resident line, as the outcome text would, is not supported by this probe. Installed (a subset of the declared outcome, decided after seeing the data for the two reasons above): the cold rule only, with constants instead of the W axis: memory.constant_cache uniform_bank0_cold_hold_cycles = 119.2 and uniform_cold_hold_cycles = 463.4 (means over the five W, measured, source kernel_start.h100.v2); a uniform-path load whose line is not resident in the SM's constant cache, or is still being filled, holds its warp at issue until the line is ready and has its result at issue; ledger reason `constant_hold`. A uniform load of a resident line keeps today's treatment (same_line / hit as result latency). Not installed: the resident hold and its values (needs cells inside and outside the recently-used range, a later version); anything on b300. The judgement declared under `install` applies unchanged.

addenda.when: after the install (engine d89c25f2 + 9f9e0bd5, build 9f9e0bd5, seven gates pass) — judgement on an H100 subset
addenda.text: The full-GPU 500 x 2 re-run named under `install` was not done: /data is at 129 GB, under the 150 GB line for a full wave. Instead every fifth H100 case (100 cases) was replayed with the new build ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sim-hold-hp100, comparison compare/hold-hp100-{base,hold}); 25 B300 cases replay to identical cycles (rule off). On the 100 cases, before -> after: site residency error mean 0.292 -> 0.281 (63 cases better, 35 worse); class attribution error 0.409 -> 0.395 (72 / 28), its outside-loop part 0.112 -> 0.100; per-pc residency error 0.985 -> 0.947 (93 / 6); imc_miss outside loops -2.15 -> -1.48 points of residency (engine still below hardware); the code outside loops before the first anchor -2.28 -> -2.23 signed, 2.64 -> 2.46 absolute. By the declared judgement the change stays (the outside-loop site error is not worse). Next to it: the cycle error gets worse, mean 0.0815 -> 0.0892, P90 0.156 -> 0.178, median sim / hardware 0.935 -> 0.925 (26 cases better, 74 worse); 87 of the 100 cases get faster, because a cold bank-0 uniform line now costs 119 at the load where it cost the 406.5 miss at its readers before. On the probe itself (g132.w8): bank 3 moves towards hardware (kernel cycles 6002 -> 9707, hardware 16089); bank 0 moves away (5703 -> 4132, hardware 7980), since the 32 re-reads that hardware holds for about 125 each are not installed. What is still missing, from this data: the first uniform loads of a kernel cost more than the steady per-line value (seed load 110-420, first bank-3 load 710-1100; deepgemm_fp8_mgroup_contiguous_06: 409 and 286), and re-reads outside the recently-used range hold as well. Both need their own cells.

addenda.when: correction of the derivation (my error), after the subset judgement and before the full-GPU run
addenda.text: The results addendum took the first 16 ULDC of the window, in listing order, as the first-touch group. ptxas interleaves the three groups (the first re-reads start after the seventh first-touch load), so that group held 7 first-touch loads and 9 re-reads, and the `resident` group held 9 first-touch loads. Groups are now told apart by the displacement of the load (first-touch loads carry the line's displacement, re-reads the table base). Corrected values, launch 0, W = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16: H_cold bank 0 128.9 / 132.4 / 130.2 / 132.0 / 133.4 (mean 131.4), bank 3 624.0 / 640.9 / 665.9 / 648.5 / 641.4 (mean 644.1); the first indexed load of the kernel 118-207 (bank 0) and 660-1105 (bank 3); H_res 118-125 on bank 0 and 115-123 on bank 3, i.e. a re-read holds about 120 on either bank (the earlier 194-216 for bank 3 was the mixture); all 24 rows usable; shares unchanged in substance. One or two re-reads per row have no sample at all (the re-read issued right after its own first touch). The reading changes on one point: bank 0's first touch (131) is still about a re-read (120), but bank 3's first touch is 644, not 465, against the installed miss 406.5. Installed values corrected to 131.4 / 644.1 (leaf and source text; engine unchanged). The subset judgement above was made with 119.2 / 463.4 and is superseded by the full-GPU run with the corrected values.

addenda.when: full-GPU 500 x 2 with the corrected values (tree 43ee2b7e, engine build 9f9e0bd5; seven gates pass on 43ee2b7e)
addenda.text: Ledgers $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/sim-ledger5, comparison compare/ledger5 against compare/ledger4m (same mapping). B300: 500 / 500 cycles identical to the baseline (rule off). H100, 500 cases, before -> after: site residency error mean 0.296 -> 0.285 (320 cases better, 173 worse); class attribution error 0.408 -> 0.394 (358 / 136), outside loops 0.128 -> 0.116; per-pc residency error 0.990 -> 0.953 (476 / 22); imc_miss outside loops -2.05 -> -1.31 points of residency; the code outside loops before the first anchor -2.18 -> -2.12 signed, 2.93 -> 2.74 absolute; constant_hold is 0.81 % of the engine's residency. By the declared judgement the change stays. Cycle error, reported next to it: MAPE 7.87 % -> 8.62 %, P90 17.1 -> 18.1, median sim / hardware 0.946 -> 0.937, cases above 20 % 24 -> 29; 429 cases get faster, 67 slower (129 closer to hardware, 367 further). The engine was already below hardware on these kernels; the rule removes time it had for a wrong reason (406.5 at the readers of every cold uniform line) and puts back less (131.4 at the load on bank 0). The hardware time still not modelled at these loads: the first uniform loads of a kernel (118-420 on the probes, 409 / 286 in the suite case) and re-reads outside the recently-used range (about 120).
